A1.justification: Despite the changed title and extensive reformatting, both PDFs describe SynthKG, its distilled model, and the proposition-entity retriever. The complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original KG coverage, retrieval, and question-answering experiments in Tables 1–4, component analyses in Figures 3–5, and human validation of generated evaluation data in Appendix B.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, human audits of generated content, and entity-distribution and filtering analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedures remain document chunking, preceding-chunk decontextualization, entity/proposition/triplet extraction, filtering, single-step distillation, and graph retrieval with optional LLM reranking. Operational prompts match across the appendices. The shortened D-SynthKG name and expanded mechanism explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both use IndustryCorpus with the same ten industry categories and evaluate on MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA. The new audits and entity analyses examine retained data or generated outputs; they introduce no distinct dataset, language, domain, or task scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds full SynthKG-8b and SynthKG-70b comparisons to KG coverage and retrieval, and GPT-4o-generated KGs to Graph+LLM retrieval. Table 3 adds GraphRAG local/drift and HippoRAG QA results. These substantially expand the evaluated comparators beyond v1's direct-prompting models and dense retrieval baselines; GraphRAG and HippoRAG were previously discussed without these reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces substantial additional evaluation procedures: inspection of 75 rewritten chunks by three authors, a separate 150-triplet audit, and GraphRAG/HippoRAG configurations with specified answer-generation controls. The existing 1,000-question benchmark setup and training budgets remain. Appendix I's 1K-token chunk description conflicts with the retained 256-token setting in Section 6.1, so an actual chunk-size change cannot be established.

E4.justification: New analyses test entity locality and the preceding-chunk assumption, decontextualization accuracy, generated-triplet precision, and ROUGE-based filtering behavior; Appendix G adds cost analysis. The existing document-length, QLoRA, retrieval-method, and input-context analyses are retained, largely relocated to Appendix B rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added audit percentages and entity-distance averages are descriptive results, without a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results appear. For example, v2 Table 1 reports 2Wiki coverage of 63.30 for SynthKG-70b versus the retained distilled-model score of 58.27. Table 3 adds average EM scores of 0.390/0.384 for GraphRAG local/drift and 0.403 for HippoRAG, versus the retained 0.433 for D-SynthKG. Audits, entity statistics, and cost estimates are added; per-dataset Hits@5 entries disappear from Table 2.

T1.justification: The KG representation and semantic matching, coverage, and F1 definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. The added mechanism explanations, descriptive analyses, and cost calculations do not constitute a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The central contributions and smaller-model performance claims are retained. However, v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion strengthen the earlier training-data hypothesis into an explicit claim that insufficient high-quality training data, rather than model capability, is the fundamental bottleneck. This changes the explanatory claim while preserving the contribution set.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments about learning consistent extraction patterns, prioritizing recall over precision, entity locality, cross-page structural limitations, and threshold selection. It removes v1 Section 9's explicit English-language and limited-model-generalization qualifications. The new locality interpretation also has an unresolved inconsistency: Section 3.1 measures distance from first mentions, whereas Appendix B.3 describes distance from the most recent mention.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed token workloads and estimated synthesis/training/inference costs, exact candidate-passage counts, evaluation-code provenance, and a promise to release synthesis/evaluation code. Existing prompts and most hyperparameters remain. The explicit Optimum-Habana/Transformers training-stack description disappears, while conflicting chunk-size and model-version descriptions in the new appendices reduce reproducibility clarity. These disclosures do not establish that experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and claim to be the first specialized LLM for ontology-free KG construction are largely retained. v2 sharpens training-resource and evaluation novelty positioning, including a first-systematic-evaluation claim, and removes the Wolf et al. Transformers reference. There is no substantial expansion of the cited research landscape.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and results around data-centric scaling and explicit research questions. It abbreviates model names, reorganizes the appendices, relocates existing analyses, and adds reproducibility and LLM-usage statements. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond additions of scientific content.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column conference layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with distinct synthesis and distillation panels; Tables 1–2 are reorganized into dataset column groups. Existing ablation plots are merged into v2 Figure 3 and moved to the appendix, alongside the density plot and Table 4. New Table 5 separately redisplays the GPT-4o retrieval comparison.

improvement.justification: The added full-pipeline and GraphRAG/HippoRAG comparisons, together with direct content-quality audits, better support the retained scientific claims. The net gain is tempered by removed scope qualifications and new documentation inconsistencies. Section 6.1 specifies 256-token chunks while Appendix I says 1K; Appendix G prices the same 14,524-token workload at both $0.0131 and $0.031, undermining its claimed 8.6% cost ratio. These weaknesses limit, but do not erase, the benefit of broader empirical validation.
